headline: Randy's Global News First — morning edition

stories.headline: OPEC+ signals a quota rethink as Brent slips below $70
stories.standfirst: Delegates say the group is weighing a slower unwind of cuts after a third straight week of falling prices.
stories.body:
Brent crude settled below $70 for the first time since spring, pushing OPEC+ delegates to open the door to a slower unwind of production cuts.

Two delegates said no decision would be taken before the next ministerial meeting, but that the group was uncomfortable with the pace of the slide.

Refiners in Asia have already trimmed term nominations for the coming quarter.

stories.headline: ECB holds rates but trims its growth path for 2027
stories.standfirst: The council kept the deposit rate unchanged while nudging down next year's growth forecast.
stories.body:
The Governing Council left rates on hold, as expected, and pointed to softer investment data across the bloc.

President's remarks stressed that policy remains restrictive enough to keep disinflation on track.

stories.headline: Tokyo opens higher as exporters shrug off a firmer yen
stories.standfirst: The Nikkei added 0.8% in the first hour, led by autos and machinery.
stories.body:
Japanese equities opened firmer despite the yen's overnight strength, with autos and machinery leading gains.

Traders pointed to bargain hunting after two sessions of losses.

stories.headline: A packaging plant in Lagos becomes Africa's first chip test site
stories.standfirst: The facility will handle final test and packaging for boards assembled in three countries.
stories.body:
The plant, financed by a mix of state and private money, will handle final test and packaging rather than wafer fabrication.

Its operators say the first commercial lots will ship within a year.

stories.headline: Brazil's soy harvest beats forecasts, easing feed costs
stories.standfirst: A record crop is arriving at port just as freight rates ease.
stories.body:
Exporters expect a record crop to clear ports without the congestion seen last season.

Feed buyers in Asia are already reporting cheaper landed costs.

stories.headline: A relay of research ships maps a new Antarctic current
stories.standfirst: Six vessels spent a season charting flows beneath the ice shelf.
stories.body:
The survey suggests a stronger inflow of warm water than models had assumed.

Results will feed into the next round of sea-level projections.
